title: High-Quality Extraction of Medium-to-Long DNA Fragments from Biogas Digestate for Nanopore Sequencing
author: He Sun

steps.title: Transfer digestate to bead tube
steps.instruction: Using a cut 1000 µL pipette tip, transfer 600 µL + 600 µL (total 1,200 µL) of homogenized digestate into an empty PowerBead Pro Tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge and weigh tube
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 10,000 × g, 20 °C for 5 min. Weigh the empty PowerBead Pro Tube and record the weight. Carefully decant the supernatant, weigh the tube again, record the weight and calculate the sample weight.

steps.title: Add CD1 and vortex
steps.instruction: Decant the beads back into the PowerBead Pro Tube. Add 800 µL of Solution CD1 and vortex briefly to mix.

steps.title: Homogenize sample
steps.instruction: Homogenize the tube in a FastPrep‑24 Classic I at 6 m/s for 20 s. Immediately place the tube on ice after lysis.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the PowerBead Pro Tube at 15,000 × g, 20 °C for 2 min. Carefully decant the supernatant into a new 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tube. Repeat this centrifugation and decanting once more.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to clean tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a clean 2 mL microcentrifuge tube (expect 500–600 µL). The supernatant may still contain some soil particles.

steps.title: Add CD2 and mix
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of Solution CD2 to the tube and mix thoroughly by gently inverting for 1 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge and transfer supernatant (first)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 15,000 × g, 20 °C for 90 s. Carefully transfer up to 700 µL of the supernatant into a clean 2.0 mL tube, avoiding disturbance of the pellet (expect 500–600 µL).

steps.title: Centrifuge and transfer supernatant (second)
steps.instruction: Repeat the previous centrifugation at 15,000 × g, 20 °C for 60 s. Transfer the remaining liquid (almost all) to a clean tube. A pellet mark may be visible on the tube wall.

steps.title: Add CD3 and mix
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL of Solution CD3 and mix thoroughly by gently inverting for 1 min. If DNA purification is planned, bring the magnetic beads to room temperature at this step.

steps.title: Load lysate onto spin column
steps.instruction: Load 650 µL of lysate onto an MB Spin Column placed in a clean 2 mL collection tube. Centrifuge at 8,000 × g, 20 °C for 1 min.

steps.title: Repeat lysate loading
steps.instruction: Discard the flow-through and repeat the loading step to ensure all lysate has passed through the MB Spin Column. Centrifuge again at 8,000 × g, 20 °C for 1 min.

steps.title: Place column in collection tube
steps.instruction: Carefully place the MB Spin Column into a clean 2 mL collection tube, avoiding splashing any flow-through onto the column.

steps.title: Wash column with EA
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of Solution EA to the MB Spin Column. Centrifuge at 8,000 × g, 20 °C for 1 min. Discard the flow-through and place the column back into the same 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with C5 (first)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of Solution C5 to the MB Spin Column. Centrifuge at 8,000 × g, 20 °C for 1 min. Discard the flow-through and place the column into a new 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Final spin and transfer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at up to 15,000 × g, 20 °C for 2 min. Carefully place the MB Spin Column into a new 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Add C6 and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 62 µL of Solution C6 to the center of the white filter membrane. Incubate for 5 min.

steps.title: Elute DNA and assess
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 8,000 × g, 20 °C for 3 min. Discard the MB Spin Column. The eluate now contains DNA ready for downstream applications. Use 1.5 µL of the eluate to assess DNA quality and estimate concentration via NanoDrop.

steps.title: Add magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Add 21 µL of magnetic beads (0.35× volume; e.g., AMPure or HighPrep) to 60 µL of DNA sample. Mix thoroughly by gentle hand shaking and flicking until beads are evenly suspended. Bring the beads to room temperature for at least 30 min before use.

steps.title: Incubate bead mixture
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Bind DNA to beads
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge the tube, then place it on a magnetic stand until the solution becomes clear and the beads are fully bound.

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: While the tube remains on the magnet, carefully remove and discard the supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol wash #1
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of freshly prepared 80 % ethanol to the beads. Incubate for 30 s. Avoid disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Additional ethanol washes
steps.instruction: Repeat the ethanol‑wash step (add 200 µL 80 % ethanol, incubate 30 s, remove supernatant) up to three times if DNA purity is insufficient, noting that excessive washing may increase DNA loss.

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge the tube, place it on the magnetic stand, and remove any residual liquid with a 10 µL pipette.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the beads for 1–2 min, avoiding over‑drying or cracking of the pellet.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL of nuclease‑free water and resuspend the beads gently by shaking and flicking until fully dispersed. Incubate at 37 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Collect purified DNA
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge the tube, place it on the magnetic stand until the solution is clear and the beads are fully bound. Collect the supernatant (30 µL DNA eluate). Use 1.5 µL for NanoDrop purity assessment, 2 µL for Qubit concentration measurement, and 5 µL for agarose‑gel fragment‑length evaluation.

steps.title: Store DNA
steps.instruction: For short‑term storage, keep the extracted DNA at 4 °C and proceed with sequencing library preparation as soon as possible.
